Sample Meeting Transcript
Project Discovery and MVP Planning Meeting
Meeting Type: Client Requirement Discussion
Date: 28 July 2026
Participants:
•
•
•
•
•
Maria — Client Founder
James — Client Operations Manager
Neha — Zignuts Business Analyst
Arjun — Zignuts Technical Lead
Riya — Zignuts UI/UX Designer
Neha: Thanks, everyone. The purpose of today’s meeting is to understand the first version of the
customer support automation platform and agree on what should be included in the MVP. Maria, could
you start by explaining the current problem?
Maria: Sure. We receive customer enquiries through email, website chat, and WhatsApp. The support
team manually reads every message, identifies the issue, and assigns it to the right person. We receive
around 800 enquiries per day, and during busy periods it can cross 1,200.
James: The biggest problem is response time. Some messages are answered within fifteen minutes, but
others remain unanswered for six or seven hours. Customers also send follow-up messages, which
creates duplicate tickets.
Neha: What would you like the new platform to automate?
Maria: Ideally, everything. It should receive messages from every channel, understand the customer’s
problem, reply automatically, assign tickets, track performance, detect unhappy customers, translate
messages, recommend refunds, and give managers complete analytics.
Arjun: That is a broad scope. For the first release, we should separate essential automation from later
enhancements. Which channels contribute the highest volume today?
James: Email is approximately 55%, website chat is 30%, and WhatsApp is the remaining 15%.
Arjun: Do you already use a ticketing system?
James: We use Zendesk, but only some teams use it correctly. A lot of communication still happens
directly through shared email inboxes.
Maria: I would prefer replacing Zendesk completely because the licence cost is high.
Neha: Replacing the complete ticketing system may significantly increase the MVP scope. Would an
initial integration with Zendesk be acceptable while we validate the AI automation?
1
Maria: Possibly, but I do not want us to become dependent on it permanently.
Arjun: We can design the integration through an adapter so that Zendesk can be replaced later. For the
MVP, that would reduce risk and avoid rebuilding ticket management, user roles, escalation workflows,
and reporting from scratch.
James: That sounds reasonable. My team mainly needs faster classification, suggested replies, and
better assignment.
Neha: Should the AI send replies automatically?
James: For simple questions, yes. For example, order status, return policy, opening hours, or password
reset instructions.
Maria: I want all messages answered automatically. The purpose of AI is to reduce the support team.
Arjun: Full automation may create business and reputational risk. The model may misunderstand
complaints, payment issues, or legally sensitive requests. We recommend confidence-based
automation. High-confidence and low-risk responses can be sent automatically. Other responses should
be drafted for human approval.
Maria: How will the system decide whether something is low risk?
Arjun: We can initially define categories. Frequently asked questions and informational requests can be
low risk. Refunds, cancellations, payment disputes, legal complaints, threats, and requests involving
personal data should require human review.
James: I agree. Refunds above €50 must already be approved by a supervisor.
Neha: That sounds like an important business rule. Does the platform need to recommend a refund, or
process it?
James: For the MVP, it should only recommend the next action. It should not directly process payments
or refunds.
Maria: Fine, but I want managers to know when customers are angry.
Riya: Would a sentiment indicator on each ticket be useful, such as positive, neutral, frustrated, or
urgent?
James: Yes, although the team should still be able to correct it because sarcasm is often misunderstood.
Arjun: Good point. We should treat sentiment as a suggestion, not an absolute result.
Neha: What information should agents see when opening a ticket?
James: Customer name, channel, original message, category, priority, sentiment, previous messages,
suggested response, and assigned agent.
2
Riya: Should agents edit the AI-generated response before sending it?
James: Yes. They should also be able to reject the suggestion and write their own response.
Maria: Can the system learn from those corrections?
Arjun: Eventually, yes. For the MVP, we can store accepted, edited, and rejected suggestions. That gives
us useful feedback data. Building an automated learning pipeline should probably be a later phase.
Maria: Okay.
Neha: Let us discuss assignment. How are tickets currently assigned?
James: Mostly manually. Billing issues go to finance support, technical issues go to the technical
support team, and account questions go to customer service. Within each team, managers assign
tickets based on availability.
Arjun: For the MVP, we could route tickets to a team based on category and leave individual assignment
manual. Automatic workload balancing could be added later.
James: That would already help.
Maria: I still want individual automatic assignment.
James: I am not sure our agent availability data is accurate enough for that.
Neha: Then perhaps the MVP can recommend an agent but require a manager or team member to
confirm the assignment.
Maria: All right, as long as we can measure how often the recommendation is accepted.
Riya: Do managers need a separate dashboard?
James: Yes. At minimum, they need total ticket volume, average first-response time, open tickets,
overdue tickets, category distribution, and the percentage of AI suggestions accepted.
Maria: I also want cost savings and customer satisfaction.
Neha: Customer satisfaction requires a feedback mechanism or existing source of CSAT data. Do you
currently collect it?
James: Zendesk sends a rating request after a ticket is closed, but response rates are low.
Neha: We can include existing CSAT data if available, but calculating accurate cost savings will require
baseline staffing and handling-time information.
Maria: Let us not delay the MVP for that. We can add detailed cost analytics later.
Arjun: Are there compliance or hosting requirements?
3
Maria: Most of our customers are in Germany and the Netherlands. Customer messages may contain
names, email addresses, order details, and sometimes addresses.
Arjun: Then GDPR and data handling are important. We need to know whether the selected AI provider
stores prompts or uses them for training. We should also avoid sending unnecessary personal data to
the model.
James: We need ticket history for at least two years.
Arjun: Storing ticket history and retaining AI processing logs are different decisions. We can retain
business records while minimizing or anonymizing model request logs.
Neha: Who will confirm the final data retention policy?
Maria: I will check with our legal consultant by Friday.
Riya: Regarding language support, which languages are required at launch?
James: English and German cover almost all enquiries.
Maria: We also receive Dutch messages.
James: Dutch volume is less than 5%.
Neha: Would English and German be acceptable for the MVP, with Dutch planned for the next release?
Maria: Yes, provided the architecture can support additional languages later.
Arjun: That is manageable.
Neha: What timeline are you expecting?
Maria: I want the MVP live in six weeks.
Arjun: Six weeks is tight if it includes three communication channels, Zendesk integration, AI
classification, response generation, sentiment analysis, multilingual support, assignment
recommendations, dashboards, and compliance work.
Maria: What can realistically be delivered?
Arjun: I suggest that the six-week MVP include email and website chat, Zendesk integration,
classification, priority detection, English and German response suggestions, confidence-based
automatic replies for approved FAQs, team-level routing, basic sentiment analysis, and a manager
dashboard.
James: What about WhatsApp?
Arjun: We can prepare the integration design but implement it in the next phase. WhatsApp
onboarding and template approval can introduce dependencies outside the development team.
4
Maria: I would prefer WhatsApp, but I understand the risk. Let us keep it out of the first release as long
as it is the first item in phase two.
Neha: Agreed. Who will provide the existing FAQ content and support response templates?
James: I can provide the FAQ documents and twenty examples of good responses by Wednesday.
Neha: We will need more than twenty examples for evaluation, especially for different categories.
James: I can ask each team lead to provide ten resolved tickets. That should give us around eighty
examples.
Arjun: Please remove or mask sensitive customer data before sharing them.
James: Understood.
Riya: I will need access to the current Zendesk workflow and screenshots of the views used by agents
and managers.
James: I will arrange a walkthrough on Thursday afternoon.
Maria: When can we see the first design?
Riya: If we receive the workflow information on Thursday, I can share initial wireframes by next
Tuesday.
Neha: Before we close, let me summarize the current direction. The MVP will not replace Zendesk. It will
integrate with it through a replaceable adapter. The first release will support email and website chat,
English and German, AI classification, priority, sentiment, suggested replies, limited automatic
responses, team routing, agent recommendations, and a basic manager dashboard. WhatsApp, Dutch
language support, automated learning, detailed cost analytics, and full replacement of Zendesk will be
considered later.
Maria: That matches my understanding.
James: Yes, but please ensure that refund-related messages are never answered automatically.
Arjun: Agreed. Refunds, payment disputes, legal complaints, data requests, and other sensitive
categories will require human review.
Neha: Maria will confirm the data retention policy with legal by Friday. James will provide FAQ
documents and anonymized ticket examples by Wednesday and arrange the Zendesk walkthrough on
Thursday. Riya will share initial wireframes by next Tuesday. Our technical team will prepare the
architecture and integration proposal after reviewing the Zendesk workflow.
Maria: Good. I would also like a revised estimate once the architecture is ready.
Arjun: We can provide that by the end of next week.
5
Neha: Perfect. We will circulate the meeting summary and action items today. Thanks, everyone.
6
